legacy_migration.trigger: A locked project-original script requires a dense explanation to remain attributable to one formal-room participant while a separate process must become visually legible; this source picture alone does not prove the explanation, technical principle, chronology or responsibility.
legacy_migration.directing_decision: Establish a complete formal-room map and a diagram/person anchor, then alternate only at state-bearing beats into an original process location, returning to the anchor before each new explanatory unit.
legacy_migration.coverage: Whole-room map → diagram/person medium → object/process insert → process receiver/group → diagram/person return → selective formal-room receiver.
legacy_migration.blocking: Lock the formal-room lectern/diagram/receiver zones and a separate original process-space map; keep each location family internally readable and do not imply identity or chronology from costume alone.
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: Begin with longer room/diagram holds; accelerate only when new visible state changes are available; reserve the densest cross-location alternation for the most consequential script-verified unit. Source durations are evidence, not a timing formula.
legacy_migration.sound: SND-UNK for this source. Any dialogue, room response, alarm, machinery, impact, fire/explosion sound, music or audio-led cut must be rebuilt from verified project-original script and sound evidence.
legacy_migration.applicability: Technical, legal, medical, procedural or family explanations where the locked script truly requires both an attributable explainer and a separately visualized process.
legacy_migration.non_applicability: Do not use when chronology must remain unknowable, the process has no filmable state changes, the explainer must be unreliable without corroboration, or one continuous demonstration already carries the necessary geography.
legacy_migration.failure_mode: Alternate location becomes decorative; viewers cannot recover the formal-room anchor; cutaway pictures falsely certify dialogue claims; chronology is accidentally asserted; diagram and process do not share state-bearing beats.
legacy_migration.counterexample: COUNTEREXAMPLE UNKNOWN: same-trigger contrary source pending. Different-trigger boundary inside this source: S200 sustains a long single-location movement after the physical-change passage, where renewed cross-location visualization would fragment the visible coda.

legacy_migration.trigger: A locked project-original script defines a measurable state crossing successive thresholds and requires several people to act on the changing state; picture alone does not establish what the numbers/lights mean or why anyone responds.
legacy_migration.directing_decision: Show the original state token in a clean insert, then distribute a sparse receiver chain from individual to pair/group before returning to a wider system view; repeat only when the token visibly changes.
legacy_migration.coverage: State-token insert → single receiver → paired receiver → hand/control insert if script-locked → group/wide state → later changed-token insert.
legacy_migration.blocking: Assign each receiver a distinct console/room zone and screen side; keep the original display position and hand side stable; stage asynchronous turns rather than a synchronized crowd response.
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: Give each changed token enough hold to read; shorten receiver fragments as threshold density rises; do not cut to every face after every number/light change.
legacy_migration.sound: SND-UNK for this source. Any dialogue, room response, alarm, machinery, impact, fire/explosion sound, music or audio-led cut must be rebuilt from verified project-original script and sound evidence.
legacy_migration.applicability: Countdowns, monitored procedures, equipment tests, medical readouts, votes or resource thresholds where the script specifies a visible state token and multiple action owners.
legacy_migration.non_applicability: Do not use for intentionally unreadable data, a single-person subjective experience, symbolic graphics with no action consequence, or scenes where hiding the threshold is the dramatic design.
legacy_migration.failure_mode: The display is unreadable; cuts repeat unchanged states; all receivers turn identically; hand inserts break side continuity; picture pretends to explain a technical value not established by the script.

legacy_migration.ai_risk: CRITICAL: camera=macro readability plus repeatable room geography; performance=distinct asynchronous receiver changes; continuity=original display values, control hand, marks and eyeline sides.
legacy_migration.fallback: Project-original locked-script fallback: one fixed newly designed numeric/shape token → one fixed receiver medium with one head turn → one fixed two-person wide with one independent posture change; omit hand contact and additional faces; lock token value and screen side.

legacy_migration.blocking: Keep process-room zones stable before escalation; in physical-event views separate foreground, source region and distant scale; do not require performers to interact with uncontrolled simulation.
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: Compress receiver shots toward the peak but let the first high/wide change and final distant view register; avoid a wall of equally short abstract fragments.

legacy_migration.failure_mode: Abstract close fragments arrive before geography; spectacle erases action ownership; simulated bodies/debris become unstable; the distant scale view is omitted; image falsely specifies the event mechanism.

legacy_migration.directing_decision: Hard-return to a planted formal-room group, rebuild the anchor through a speaker/raised-desk/receiver triangle, permit one materially longer movement/hold, and end on a whole-room map before the next scene.
legacy_migration.coverage: Formal-room group → central participant → raised-desk receiver → paired/table receiver → longer participant movement/hold → selective rows → whole-room end frame.
legacy_migration.blocking: Restore previously established formal-room zones and screen sides; keep most bodies planted; reserve the long movement for one script-locked participant and allow a foreground body to occlude only after axis is clear.
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: After the peak, widen average duration and reduce cut frequency; use only distinct receiver zones; let the final whole-room view settle before crossing into the next location. Source timings are not a formula.
legacy_migration.sound: SND-UNK for this source. Any dialogue, room response, alarm, machinery, impact, fire/explosion sound, music or audio-led cut must be rebuilt from verified project-original script and sound evidence.
legacy_migration.applicability: Hearings, briefings, debriefs, family councils or command-room codas where the locked script requires accountability/consequence after a visualized event.
legacy_migration.non_applicability: Do not use when the scene ends at the physical peak, aftermath ownership belongs entirely to another location, the formal room has not been established, or rapid procedural action must continue.
legacy_migration.failure_mode: Return feels like a reset with no restored geography; too many receiver singles repeat information; the long hold loses a script-verified action; final wide arrives after the next scene has already begun; picture labels guilt or authority without evidence.
